name: None Up
summary: The Tallymen's Great Dredge west of Isseva dug down to a Builders' street under the peat, and three weeks ago its whole crew went down the shaft at the change of shift and none came up. Wenna Corley, the crew's cook and tally-keeper, keeps the pot on for fourteen and wants the dredge-master's tally brought up, so the board can be closed.
notes: Sedgemire novel places (2026-10-04): the Great Dredge (core:poi/the_great_dredge, core:interior/the_great_dredge_workings, Brannoc Tull as its boss). The plate the boss drops leads out to core:quest/the_line_on_the_needle at the Flood-Mark.

stages.journal: Wenna Corley's crew went down the Great Dredge's shaft three weeks ago and none came up; she wants Brannoc Tull's tally brought up so the board can close. The ladder is at the landward side of the shaft. Below it are the Guild's cuttings, the night men's camp, and the Builders' street they broke into, and at the bottom of it all the dredge-master, Brannoc Tull, who always was.

objectives.text: Find Brannoc Tull at the bottom of the shaft
Take the dredge-master's tally from his belt

stages.journal: Brannoc Tull's tally came up out of the shaft with a Builders' plate wired to it, and Wenna Corley needs somebody not Guild to say what the Dredge does now. She is at the crew's fire by the shaft. The Guild will want the Dredge digging again by the spring with a new crew; or the pin can come out of the sheer-legs' head and the chain go down the shaft for good.

objectives.text: Tell Wenna Corley what becomes of the Great Dredge

options.text: Knock the pin out of the sheer-legs' head and let the chain go down the shaft for good.
Give the tally to the Guild and let them send a new crew down.
Keep the tally and say nothing to anybody.

stages.journal: That night the bucket-chain hung still in the shaft from dusk to dawn, and in the morning Wenna Corley moved the pegs on the tally-board for the last time.

name: The Line on the Needle
summary: The Builders' plate that came up the Great Dredge's shaft is cut with the same line as the black needle at the Flood-Mark, and Hesk Vaurel, the last Tide-Watcher, reads the Builders' marks.
notes: Sedgemire novel places (2026-10-04): leads out of the Great Dredge (core:quest/the_great_dredge) to the Flood-Mark (core:poi/the_flood_mark). The plate is handed over by the next conversation with Hesk (QuestRoutes).

stages.journal: Wenna Corley says the Builders' plate from the shaft bears the Flood-Mark needle's own line, and Hesk Vaurel at Oulea reads Builders' marks. The Flood-Mark stands at the channel's edge below Oulea: a black needle four storeys tall with a white gauge up its face, and the Tide-Watcher's hut on the bank.

objectives.text: Bring the Builders' plate to Hesk Vaurel at the Flood-Mark

stages.journal: Hesk Vaurel has had her night with the plate and a candle, and wants you to say what is done with what it says. The line is the flood, she says, and the marks either side of it are a count of tides, and the count is not finished.

objectives.text: Tell Hesk Vaurel what is done with the plate

options.text: Cut the plate's line into the gauge, so the watchers know what they are watching for.
Drop the plate down the float-well, where the water can keep it.
Send the plate to the Reed Council at Isseva; it is theirs to tell.

stages.journal: At the next spring tide Hesk Vaurel notched the gauge as she always had, and put her mark beside it, and sat on the wet bench until the ebb with her boots on.

name: The Keel-Barrow
summary: Hesk Vaurel, the last Tide-Watcher, has measured the stem of the Salt Isles' ship-barrow on the flats turning toward the sea a finger a night. By the next spring tide it will point straight out, and the drowned already muster at its side.
notes: Sedgemire novel places (2026-10-04): the Keel-Barrow (core:poi/the_keel_barrow, core:interior/the_keel_barrow_hold, Hrothe Tidecaller as its boss). A ropewalker's token on the oar-benches leads out to core:quest/iven_hasks_rope at Hask's Ropewalk.

stages.journal: Hesk Vaurel has measured the Keel-Barrow's stem turning toward the sea a finger a night, and by the spring tide it will point straight out. The barrow is on the flats past the Saltgate, the ship's posts standing out of its ends; the door is in her landward side. Whatever is turning her is in the hold, at the steering-oar.

objectives.text: Go to the Keel-Barrow on the flats past the Saltgate
Put down the Keel-King at his steering-oar
Take the steering-pin from the oar's head

stages.journal: The Keel-King's steering-pin came out of the oar cold and wet and with it gone the stem has stopped, so Hesk Vaurel must say what is done with it. She is at the Flood-Mark. It can be driven back into the stem-post to moor the ship for good, or given to the sea with the mooring-rope cut, so the ship points home.

objectives.text: Tell Hesk Vaurel what is done with the steering-pin

options.text: Drive the pin into the stem-post, so the ship stays moored where she lies.
Cut the mooring-rope and give the pin to the sea at the ebb.

stages.journal: That night the drowned did not come up the flats to the Keel-Barrow's side, and in the morning the mooring-stake stood straight.

name: For Iven Hask, When He Comes Home
summary: On the Keel-King's oar-benches lay a ropewalker's token stamped HASK. Corra Hask's brother Iven went down to the Outfall nine years ago to ship with a Salt Isles boat and never came home; his rope is still on her rack.
notes: Sedgemire novel places (2026-10-04): leads out of the Keel-Barrow (the token is an item feature in core:interior/the_keel_barrow_hold's oar_benches) to Hask's Ropewalk, and back to the barrow if the rope is to be laid there.

stages.journal: A ropewalker's token stamped HASK lay among the Keel-King's oarsmen, and Corra Hask's brother Iven went to sea nine years ago and never came home. Hask's Ropewalk is on the peat island west of the Lantern Causeway: the long line of trestles, the wheel under its lean-to.

objectives.text: Take the ropewalker's token from the Keel-Barrow's oar-benches
Bring the token to Corra Hask at the ropewalk

stages.journal: Corra Hask knows now where her brother is, and the rope on her rack with his name in it can go to him. She will either have it carried to the barrow and laid where his crew musters, or walk his name into every rope she makes.

objectives.text: Tell Corra Hask what becomes of Iven's rope

options.text: Carry Iven's rope to the Keel-Barrow and lay it where his crew musters.
Let her walk his name into every rope she makes.

stages.journal: Corra Hask has given you Iven's named rope to lay at the Keel-Barrow, where the drowned muster at the ship's side. Lay it on the turf by the stem, tied to nothing.

objectives.text: Lay Iven's rope at the Keel-Barrow

stages.journal: From then on every rope that came off Hask's wheel had Iven Hask's name walked into it first, and there was not a boat in Isseva that was not tied up with him.

name: The First Cord
summary: Iffo Nauve has been thinking about the Name-Wife: she said she gave her own name first, to see if it could be done. Then the first cord she ever knotted is her own name, and it is still in her hollow, and a name nobody remembers can only be let go at the Unwinding.
notes: Sedgemire novel places (2026-10-04): leads out of the Name-Wife's Hollow (the first cord is a note feature in its secret room, core:item/note_name_wifes_first_cord) to the Unwinding (core:poi/the_unwinding), walked to its middle (a reach with a 3 m radius: only the pool inside the innermost ring is within it), decided with Edda Moye at the gate.

stages.journal: Iffo Nauve says the Name-Wife gave her own name first, so the first cord she ever knotted is hers, and it will still be in her hollow. Her hollow is under the South Scarp. The first cord will be where she kept what mattered: behind the loose stones.

objectives.text: Find the Name-Wife's first cord in her hollow

stages.journal: Iffo Nauve says a name nobody remembers can only be let go at the Unwinding, so the first cord must be walked to its middle. The Unwinding is the reed maze south of Nauvissa: in at the gate, five times round, to the pool and the grief-stone at the middle.

objectives.text: Walk the Unwinding to the pool at its middle

stages.journal: The first cord has been walked to the middle of the Unwinding, and Edda Moye at the gate asks what is to be done with it. It can be said into the pool and let go, tied on the pole with the walkers' ribbons unsaid, or kept.

objectives.text: Tell Edda Moye what is done with the first cord

options.text: Say it into the pool and let the water have it.
Tie it on the pole with the ribbons, unsaid but kept.

stages.journal: That night in Nauvissa the grey did not come over the scarp at all, and Iffo Nauve dreamed of a small girl tying her first knot, very badly, and laughing.
